name: py-ballisticcalc
description: Ballistic solver library for small arms: point-mass 3-DoF plus spin drift, adaptive RK45 integrators, multiple ballistic coefficients and custom drag functions.
data_sources: Own physics implementation; traces its model to Robert McCoy's Modern Exterior Ballistics and Bryan Litz's Applied Ballistics.
usefulness: The most complete solver found and the natural cross-check for our own drag code. Would give independent validation of packages/ballistics-core rather than a replacement.
adopt_reason: LGPL-3.0 is a poor fit for our deployment. Linking it into a distributed frontend triggers copyleft obligations, and it is Python with C extensions, not something to run in a Cloudflare Workers edge runtime. Use as an offline oracle in a test harness, never as shipped code.
warnings: Its README carries an explicit risk notice: results MUST NOT be considered reliable where incorrect calculation could cause financial harm or endanger a human life.

name: js-ballistics
description: JavaScript/TypeScript ballistics library powered by a C++ core compiled to WebAssembly. Same 3-DoF plus spin-drift model.
data_sources: Same physics lineage as py-ballisticcalc; part of the shared Ballistics Lab ecosystem.
usefulness: Permissive licence, TypeScript-native, ships a WASM build. The only candidate found that could plausibly run inside our actual deployment target. Also exposes DragTables, directly relevant to our drag dataset.
adopt_reason: ISC permits use, modification and redistribution with attribution and no copyleft obligation, and it matches our runtime. This is adopt=yes while the better-known py-ballisticcalc is adopt=no because of licensing and deployment, not quality.
warnings: Same risk notice as py-ballisticcalc: educational use, not a basis for anything where a wrong answer could harm someone.

name: ammolytics/projectiles
description: Open dataset of ammunition projectile (bullet) information, shipped as a thin JS wrapper over JSON.
usefulness: Would give bullet dimensional data for manufacturers we do not carry, most usefully the European names we lack. Useful as a cross-check on our bullet diameters, not as a source of ballistic coefficients.
adopt_reason: MIT is permissive and this is static dimensional data, which does not decay the way a load table does. Adopting it as a cross-check is low risk and closes part of our bullet-coverage gap.
warnings: Stated work in progress, 9 stars and 2 forks. Treat as incomplete, not authoritative.

name: ammolytics/cartridges
description: Open dataset of cartridge information drawn from SAAMI, CIP and NATO STANAG.
data_sources: Explicitly SAAMI, CIP and NATO STANAG.
usefulness: The most useful single resource found for cartridge naming and aliases, particularly CIP and NATO designations we do not carry. We hold 318 cartridges; this would extend coverage without paying a standards body.
adopt_reason: MIT is permissive and this is exactly the naming-and-dimension data we lack. Low risk, real coverage gain. Not adopted for pressure data, which it does not carry.
warnings: Stated work in progress; the author notes only SAAMI and CIP names are listed so far. Verify any dimension against the standards body before publishing it.

name: zen/grt_databases
description: Calibers, projectiles, powder models and user-contributed load data shared by Gordons Reloading Tool Discord users.
data_sources: Discord users, collected for convenience. Each record carries the sharing user and date.
usefulness: Potentially the largest free corpus of community load data anywhere, which is otherwise a paid-manual problem. Could feed reload-vs-buy cost models.
adopt_reason: The licence permits use, but this is USER-CONTRIBUTED LOAD DATA from a chat forum and the author explicitly disclaims responsibility and says measurements must be verified. Our stated position is that reloading recommendations come from manufacturer-published data, not crowdsourced numbers. Publishing a load from here could hurt someone.
warnings: CC0-1.0, the most permissive licence available, AND the author disclaims responsibility and states measurements must be verified. The clearest case in this dataset that a permissive licence is not a quality signal. Only 5 commits.

name: SAAMI Z299 series
description: ANSI American National Standards for cartridge and chamber dimensions and for pressure and velocity of rimfire, shotshell, centrefire pistol and centrefire rifle ammunition.
data_sources: Is the standards body, so this is the primary source rather than a dataset.
usefulness: The authoritative source for the pressure ceiling of every cartridge we list. Z299.4 is the centrefire rifle standard, currently the 2025 revision.
adopt_reason: The standards are sold, not open, and SAAMI states their content is intended for commercial manufacturers. Our pressure data is therefore recorded as `derived` from secondary compilations rather than `published`, which is why value_provenance marks the .308 maximum as derived and not published. Purchase access only if we need to upgrade a figure.
warnings: Paywalled. SAAMI also states it cannot advise on propellant selection, charge weights or primer choice and directs handloaders to manuals and manufacturers, so it would not close the load-data gap even if bought.

name: SAAMI new and revised cartridge and chamber drawings
description: Free PDF drawings for newly accepted SAAMI cartridge and chamber designs not yet in a published standard, plus pending dimensional corrections to existing designs.
usefulness: Free and genuinely useful: covers designs such as 21 Sharp, 25 Creedmoor, 7mm Backcountry, 8.6 Blackout and 30 Super Carry that may post-date our dataset, and it carries pending corrections to existing drawings.
adopt_reason: Free to download and published by the standards body itself, so it is primary evidence. The caution is that these are pre-standard: an accepted design not yet in a published Z299 revision must be recorded as such.
warnings: Not yet incorporated into the SAAMI Standards and subject to change at the next revision. Also holds REVISIONS to existing drawings, and a dimensional correction not yet folded into the standard is exactly what silently invalidates a figure we already hold.
